### 2026-10-11 – Hi there,

**7h**

Hi there,
It may have taken me my whole weekend but I finished everything.

I decided to make my starbie more rabbit looking.
This was my first hardware project so I am extremely proud of it.

The guide was right, there are some excellent youtube videos on Kikad, which helped me alot. (including me realising that labels and text are not the same thing 🤦‍♂️)

Thanks for this opportunity,
Joel

### 2026-10-23 – Sooo, I kind of messed up, I thought that If I didn't submit anything in the first week I couldn't continue anymore, but it turned out to be ok. When I started work on the second week I decided to fin

**4h**

Sooo, I kind of messed up, I thought that If I didn't submit anything in the first week I couldn't continue anymore, but it turned out to be ok. When I started work on the second week I decided to finish off this project and make it A LOT better than before.

Anyway, here is what I have done these past few days:
1. New design:
![IMG_8478](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RfTob6dK90218aTtBc3n7K6Xwio9QKuG/cb409e73807777f37b2605326be2e43af15c8beeb035f03ea1b4c26b3b9e7ce9.jpg)
When I originally started I drafted out this plan that I thought I could build, unfortunately, since I have no skills it was impossible for me, so I did a rabbit spin of the original starbie. However, in that first week I was able to push up my skills much faster than I thought, so I decided to build my original project for real. That was what I submitted for week 2.
2. Put it into a schematic:
I modified the original schematic from starbie to fit my new project. I found a cheap presence sensor on Aliexpress that could track up to three people (perfect for my idea of a moving around game), a CO2 sensor with Temperature and Humidity monitoring (reminding me to open a window to turn on the aircon when I need it), I also have a few LED's to make everything look pretty and quickly alter me of anything (as well as visual feedback when you press the buttons).

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 090602](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RfTob6dK90218aTtBc3n7K6Xwio9QKuG/ff0a052fa7f995e2435cd5dbcd052ab3f2de8fbad1c15ff1eca0bc6efe308e6c.png)
Along with the help of multiple youtube videos, guides and AI's, I was able to make up a proper pcb (with auto tracing help from freerouting):

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 090508](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RfTob6dK90218aTtBc3n7K6Xwio9QKuG/d483b123bd7e3ef1cf3d4d897a01cb9469cae8064ff15da8f4e6b5d4e1e77bcf.png)
The PCB was the hardest things to make as it had to go through several iterations back and forth from jlcpcb telling me something was wrong and then not really elaborating.

Seeing the finalised PCB was really cool, I honestly couldn't believe that I had built that  myself.

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 082713](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RfTob6dK90218aTtBc3n7K6Xwio9QKuG/d0a1b97cadde9663a2a779939e4a897ea1b9e9c556a11cc0162660ea02ac9c8d.png)

The only thing I have not completed is the code, it is currently still the stock starbie one (dw I will get around to finishing it off). I am currently in my exam studying period with my final exams in two weeks so I have not had much time to focus on this project unfortunately.

I also have one question:
I already bought everything that I need, including ordering the PCB from Jlcpcb and parts from aliexpress, does that mean I cannot receive funding for this project?

Thanks!
